overall_reasoning: Live triage on the Black Hat XSIAM tenant was dominated by Large Upload and scanner noise. The highest-scoring new case was a zone-protection Host Sweep. Rather than chase volume, I opened it because Host Sweep claims are either real recon or high-value false positives — both teach multi-source IR. Alert remotes were public DNS on port 53 from {{ZONE_FROM}}. Deep host identify showed an agentless Mac with privacy MAC, hostname only {{HOSTNAME_A}}, Kandji MDM, Corelight enterprise + BH NOC Slack, and consumer SaaS. BH map empty (not training 10.220). Related alerts were mostly Monitored Thread noise. XQL threats were informational TLS only. Conclusion: false positive with high confidence; no containment.

final_findings.summary: Primary: {{CASE_PRIMARY}} Host Sweep is a false positive — {{HOST_A}} queried public DNS ({{DNS_GOOGLE}}, {{DNS_QUAD9}}) from {{ZONE_FROM}}; not internal recon.
Host {{HOST_A}} / MAC {{MAC_A}} is agentless Apple-class (hostname {{HOSTNAME_A}}); org fingerprints include Corelight + BH NOC Slack and Kandji; no person name in telemetry.
No credible TP in open top-N at hunt time; Large Upload class remains scorer-demoted noise. Disposition: recommend FP resolve, do not isolate.

Outbound mostly 443. Threats informational (ECH, hybrid PQ ciphers). enrich on {{DNS_GOOGLE}} showed many source hosts — public resolver, not unique IoC. TP hypothesis collapsed.

Public DNS widely used on tenant

step-05-disposition.reasoning: Multi-source agreement: alert semantics (public DNS), identity (agentless Mac), traffic (SaaS/MDM), related (noise), threats (info). Recommend false_positive resolve with written disproof. Do not isolate. Confidence ~0.85. No mutation executed without human confirm.
findings: Ruled out: internal recon, C2, training-room compromise, named human ID
